method: Audio (measure.py -> measured.json): real local components on this 2 vCPU x86 VM: openWakeWord hey_jarvis, silero-vad (300 ms hangover) and webrtcvad, sherpa-onnx Whisper tiny.en and streaming zipformer, Piper low voices. Test audio: 25 commands x 3 Piper voices + 5 Season 1 household lines, each after a synthetic 'Hey Jarvis', in three conditions (clean; series narration through a TV-speaker EQ at 10 dB and 0 dB below the command); 6 commands split by a 0.3-0.9 s pause, endpointed at 300/500/800 ms hangover; 8.7 min of narration, assistant voices and music through the TV EQ for wake-word false accepts; 12 cases of the TV itself saying the wake word. Transcripts are re-scored by the B05 grammar in run.py. Twin (run.py): per tier, N seeded sessions on a fresh B01 twin; three utterances 25 s apart drawn from the measured clips (their transcript, wake result and endpoint delay), the cut-off set and the TV-wake set; stage times drawn from the tier table (this CPU measured; other tiers labelled assumptions); B01 PolicyEngine and ActionTracker decide and confirm; ground truth = the twin device's physical state when 'Done' is heard. Time to first audio = end of the person's speech to the first reply audio (question, hold line, answer or 'Done'); the earcon after the wake word is reported apart.

limitations: All speech is synthetic (Piper, espeak phonemes, and the Season 1 synthetic voices); no human speakers, no real room, no far-field microphone. Accuracy numbers will be worse with real voices and rooms.

TV-like speech is the series narrator and assistant voices through an EQ, mixed digitally; no acoustic echo cancellation was modelled, which a real satellite would use against its own TV/speaker output.
Only 8.7 minutes of TV-like audio: zero false accepts bounds the rate only below about 21 per hour (95%).
The Pi 5, mini PC and GPU tiers are not measured: they scale this CPU's measured numbers or reuse B01 assumptions, as labelled per stage.

This CPU was shared with other jobs during measure.py: Whisper tiny decode (p50 396 ms) and Piper first audio (p50 360 ms) are slower than B01's unloaded measurement on the same machine (166 ms, 87 ms).
No LLM was run: model weights are hosted on huggingface.co, blocked here. The LLM path is a deterministic fuzzy matcher with assumed LLM latency.
Every tier uses the same Whisper tiny transcripts; a larger STT model on the GPU tier would likely make fewer errors.
Voice identity is a fixed confidence of 0.9 for household voices (speaker ID is episode B06).
Fault, TV and cut-off rates in the twin are scenario parameters; the per-case outcome shares are what the run measures.
